note: THE SURFACE WE TRAIN ON. Derived from Vesta's production tool registry — every tool here is one the app can dispatch today, with the argument names and types the dispatcher actually expects. v1 was the Needle spike's four-tool toy schema and is frozen as historical eval material; training against it would have spent GPU time teaching an interface we already knew we were replacing.

outcomes.tool: An executable action: every REQUIRED argument present AND grounded in the user's own words.
outcomes.incomplete: The request names a tool but a required argument has no evidence in what the user said. NOT an action — Vesta asks.
outcomes.cancel: The user abandoned or cancelled a pending action.
outcomes.chat: No action. The request belongs to the conversational model.

chatIsNotATool: Vesta's registry contains a `general_chat` tool, and it is deliberately NOT listed below. Carrying it as a selectable tool would make 'chat' both a tool and a non-tool outcome, so every no-tool case could be scored two ways and the false-positive-action rate would depend on which. The router emits the `chat` OUTCOME; mapping that onto `general_chat` at dispatch is Vesta's business.

tools.name: set_alarm
tools.description: Set an alarm at a specific time.

date.description: Only when the user named a day other than today.
date.note: Optional, and it must stay optional. A required date is a date the model fills in — the confabulation Vesta's scheduling guard exists to stop. A date the user never said is refused at dispatch whatever the model proposes.

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create a calendar event or appointment.

tools.name: set_reminder
tools.description: Create a reminder with a notification at a specific time.
tools.note: Two required arguments, one of them temporal. The most common missing-slot shape on this surface is a reminder with a text and no time, or a time and no text.

minutes.description: Timer duration in minutes, greater than zero.
minutes.note: MINUTES, not seconds. This is the single most consequential difference between v1 and v2. The spike's headline failure — 'Set a timer for 20 minutes.' answered with duration_seconds: 20, a 60x error — does not transfer: against THIS schema the answer 20 is correct. The unit risk is real but different, and it is the conversions that are now the hard cases: '90 seconds' is 1.5, 'two hours' is 120, 'half an hour' is 30.

tools.name: navigate_to
tools.description: Start navigation to a destination using the maps app.

destination.description: Address or place name, in the user's own words.

tools.name: search_contacts
tools.description: Search the address book for a contact by name.

tools.name: make_call
tools.description: Start a phone call to a contact or number.
tools.note: Destructive and irreversible in the way that matters: a call that should not have been placed has already rung somebody. Its false-positive cases carry the `high-cost` tag and are weighted accordingly.

tools.name: send_sms
tools.description: Compose an SMS to a contact or number.
tools.note: Also `high-cost`. A fabricated message body is worse than a fabricated room in every way.

tools.name: get_calendar_events
tools.description: Read calendar events for a date.

date.description: Day to read; omit for today.
date.note: Optional on purpose, and a case in its own right. 'What's on my calendar?' names no day. The correct answer is the tool with NO date, which Vesta resolves to today at dispatch — not a date the model invented.

tools.name: query_document
tools.description: Search the user's imported documents and answer from their content.

tools.name: get_time
tools.description: Read the current time or date, here or in another place or time zone.

place.description: City, country or IANA zone; omit for the device's own.

tools.note: No required arguments, so it cannot produce a missing-slot case. Note that Vesta's deterministic world-time layer answers most of these BEFORE any model runs; the router sees this tool only for what that layer declined.

notInThisVersion.general_chat: Represented as the `chat` outcome — see chatIsNotATool.
notInThisVersion.control_light: v1 toy tool. Home Assistant routing is on Vesta's roadmap and is not dispatchable today.
notInThisVersion.open_app: v1 toy tool. App launching is not in the production registry.
notInThisVersion.mcp: Vesta exposes a read-only MCP server; routing OUT to MCP servers is roadmap.
notInThisVersion._rule: A tool the app cannot dispatch does not belong in the schema the model is trained on. Adding one teaches the router to propose actions that can only be refused, and every such proposal is indistinguishable from a false positive at scoring time.
